SEVERITY: costly. RECURRING -- three separate firings within one task.

CITATIONS -- specs/328_systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency/issues.jsonl:
  iss_1793841635583_gpNhE6 (dispatch_seq 18, Phase 7 -- 47 of 48 migrated test files dropped)
  iss_1793847274112_byw6XR (dispatch_seq 20, Phase 8 -- 51 touched paths dropped)
  iss_1793848518784_26KAZz (dispatch_seq 21, Phase 9 -- 2 paths dropped, one of them manifest.json)

LIVE SYMPTOM: git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check drops a legitimately-required manifest.json registration from a phase-closing commit. A phase that extracts a new shared shell library into agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/lib/ must ALSO register that lib in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts -- scripts/tests/test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh enforces that pairing mechanically. But the containment predicate reads the manifest.json path as a file_scope excursion and drops it, so the phase closes with an incomplete commit and has to pay a separate labeled follow-up commit to recover. Observed in Phase 9 (the install-extension / uninstall-extension pair) and again, identically, in Phase 10 (the typst pair).

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED -- DO NOT RE-FIX IT (verified in the source store while creating this record; re-derive before editing, line numbers move):
- All three cited entries attribute the drop to a DOUBLE-SLASH glob defect: a trailing-slash file_scope directory entry composing "${entry}/*" into "...tests//*", which never matches a real single-slash child path. THAT DEFECT IS CLOSED. agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-phase.sh's is_contained() (around lines 272-305) normalizes a trailing-slash entry down to a bare directory via a `while [ "${entry%/}" != "$entry" ]` loop before composing any glob, and its own comment documents exactly the failure mode those citations describe.
- An engine-written-paths allowlist is also in place: is_contained()'s file_scope array is pre-seeded from lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh, with a hardcoded ("specs/TODO.md", "specs/state.json") pair as the fallback on a source failure.
The citations are therefore retained as the evidence of RECURRENCE and of cost, NOT as a live description of the mechanism. Read them for the cost account, not for the diagnosis.

THE ACTUAL OPEN QUESTION -- a manifest.json registration is a STRUCTURALLY DERIVABLE obligation, not an unforeseeable newly-discovered path. When a phase adds a file under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/, that extension's own manifest.json registration is required BY A TEST, in the same change. Decide and implement ONE coherent rule, with the reasoning recorded:
(1) Make the containment predicate treat the touched extension's own manifest.json as implicitly in scope whenever the same phase adds or removes a file under that same extension's scripts/ tree. Narrow, mechanically derivable, and prevents the FIRST drop rather than only the repeat. Weigh against: it widens declared territory without review, and file_scope is also the batch admission gate's conflict-detection input and the territory contract between concurrently dispatched tasks.
(2) Surface the obligation as a PRE-COMMIT requirement instead of an implicit widening -- a phase that adds a script under an extension without also touching that extension's manifest.json is told so before the commit fires, leaving the declaration honest and the operator in the loop.
(3) Neither, on the grounding that the general declaration-staleness feedback mechanism (see the territory edges below) subsumes this case once it lands. If this is the ruling, record it explicitly and close this record rather than leaving it open.

NOTE ON THE TASK-LOCAL WORKAROUND: the symptom was worked around for one task alone by widening that task's own declared file_scope (commit 059e41377, which added agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json and agent-system/extensions/typst/manifest.json to it). That workaround is per-task and does not generalize -- the next task that extracts a lib under a different extension hits the same drop with no declaration covering it. Do not mistake the widened file_scope for a fix.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT weaken the containment predicate for a genuine excursion. Drop-and-warn for an out-of-territory source edit is correct and must survive intact, pinned by a test.
- Do NOT make the check fatal. Fail-open on a missing/empty/malformed file_scope, and never refusing a whole commit over this guard, are both deliberate and must stay.
- Any state.json write must go through the mutex-guarded state-write.sh path, never a second writer.
- Do NOT re-introduce the trailing-slash normalization or the engine-written-paths allowlist; both are already present and must be left working.

VERIFY: extend agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh with fixtures pinning (a) the chosen rule's behaviour for a phase that adds a new script under an extension plus that extension's manifest.json, (b) a genuinely out-of-territory path STILL dropped with its warning and its issue-record.sh call, (c) fail-open behaviour on absent/empty/malformed file_scope unchanged, and (d) the trailing-slash normalization still working.

TERRITORY EDGES -- git-commit-phase.sh is SHARED FILE TERRITORY with three open records, so dependency edges are declared rather than racing them (context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md: shared territory is serialized with an edge, never a bare exclusion):
- feed_undeclared_implement_paths_into_file_scope: the general form of this exact problem -- feeding observed-but-undeclared implement paths back into the declaration. If its general mechanism lands first, THIS record may reduce to option (3) above, or to a narrow prevention rule layered on top. Read its description before scoping; it already carries a verified account of git-commit-phase.sh's drop site and of the proposed_file_scope channel.
- close_the_plan_to_file_scope_reconciliation_gap: owns the plan-to-file_scope harvest path (plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, skill-base.sh) and makes a containment drop non-advisory. A manifest.json registration is exactly the kind of path a plan's "Files to modify" block may or may not name, so the two interact directly.
- collapse_perpath_scope_excursion_issue_rows_into_one: rewrites the per-path issue-record.sh emission inside the very loop this record changes.

=== SCOPE NOTE: THIS RECORD IS THE UNCOVERED REMAINDER, NOT THE GENERAL PROBLEM ===

The originating change request was framed as the general file_scope-staleness problem with two candidate resolutions (a sanctioned in-dispatch file_scope extension path, versus a containment predicate that accepts a newly-created file under an already-declared parent). A duplicate check performed at creation time established that BOTH framings are already owned, and that three of the four issue ids the request cited are already cited by an existing record:

- #430 (feed_undeclared_implement_paths_into_file_scope) owns the general in-dispatch extension channel, including the proposed_file_scope-extended-to-implement option, the auto-merge-versus-operator-confirmation ruling, and the concurrent-territory-contract constraint. It already cites iss_1792191089627_HbXkDD.
- #486 (stop a required extension manifest.json registration being dropped) owns the extension-manifest half, including the "treat the touched extension's own manifest.json as implicitly in scope" option. It already cites iss_1793841635583_gpNhE6, iss_1793847274112_byw6XR and iss_1793848518784_26KAZz, and it already records the typst-phase recurrence.
- #446 owns the plan-to-file_scope harvest reconciliation and the unread-warning half; #484 owns the per-path issue-row fan-out that produces the large "scope excursion" counts; #494 owns the own-artifact-directory member at the phase-commit site; completed #469 landed the shared engine-written-state allowlist.

No new record was created for the general problem. What remains genuinely unowned is below: it is specific to the CYCLE-POSTFLIGHT containment site and to the recovery commit, neither of which any record above names.

=== EVIDENCE (this run, cycle 1, dispatch_seq 24) ===

orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh emitted EXCURSION DROPPED for two paths and reported "2 of 11 reported modified_files entries were dropped from this cycle's commit as file_scope excursions":

    agent-system/extensions/literature/manifest.json
    agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/lib/literature_search_pylib.py

Both were real, chartered work: the phase extracted a shared python library and registered it in that extension's manifest. The dispatch recovered them in a separate labeled follow-up commit, ff880f77259fffd64836f373350710e0b5d1d7b0 ("task 328 phase 11: collapse literature-search.sh's self-internal repetition (follow-up commit)"), which carries exactly those two files and 334 insertions.

SCOPING ACCURACY, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVERSTATED LATER: the 127 entries of class "scope excursion" in specs/328_systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency/issues.jsonl are CUMULATIVE across that task's whole history, not from this run. In this run only cycle 1 hit the condition; cycles 2 and 3 both reported clean containment. This is a recurring structural gap, not an every-phase failure.

=== MECHANICS VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE STORE AT CREATION TIME (re-derive before editing; line numbers move) ===

FINDING 1 -- THE DROP FIRED AT A SITE NO OPEN RECORD OWNS. context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's "Three Containment sites, not one" section (around line 342) names site 1 as orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's WORK (h)/(i) filter, site 2 as git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check, and site 3 as V10 inside git-commit-scoped.sh. The EXCURSION DROPPED string exists at exactly one place in the corpus, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh (WORK (i), around line 1954), so the observed drop is a SITE 1 event. Every open record listed in the scope note above declares git-commit-phase.sh (site 2) and/or git-commit-scoped.sh (site 3) in its file_scope; NONE declares orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh. #486's file_scope is exactly four paths -- git-commit-phase.sh, its test, general-implementation-agent.md, git-staging-scope.md -- and its VERIFY section extends only test-git-commit-phase.sh. So whatever manifest-registration rule #486 lands will NOT reach the site where this drop actually happened.

FINDING 2 -- THE TWO SITES DO NOT RUN THE SAME PREDICATE, THOUGH THE STANDARD SAYS THEY DO. git-staging-scope.md calls it "the same Containment predicate ... checked at three independent sites". It is not the same predicate:
- Site 1 (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, around lines 1689-1690) tests `$p == $f or ($p | startswith($f))`. Bare startswith, with no path-boundary check and no trailing-slash normalization.
- Site 2 (git-commit-phase.sh's is_contained(), around lines 272-305) normalizes a trailing-slash entry down to a bare directory via a `while [ "${entry%/}" != "$entry" ]` loop and then composes a `"${entry}/*"` glob.
Two consequences follow, in OPPOSITE directions, and both are live today. Site 1 OVER-matches: a declared entry `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts` admits `agent-system/extensions/core/scripts-archive/x.sh`, because startswith has no `/` boundary. Site 1 also does not share site 2's trailing-slash normalization, so the two sites can disagree about the same path against the same declaration. Task 328's own declaration is the worked example: it holds `agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/tests/` (trailing slash, matched at site 1 only by accident of startswith) and `agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/literature-search.sh`, but neither `.../scripts/lib/` nor `.../manifest.json` -- so the two dropped paths are genuine non-members at both sites, while the predicates' agreement on OTHER paths is coincidental rather than guaranteed.

FINDING 3 -- THE RECOVERY ROUTE HAS NO CONTAINMENT GUARANTEE. Site 3 (V10 inside git-commit-scoped.sh) is `--task <N>` opt-in only. Its own header (around lines 461-472) states that `containment_scope_arr` is left EMPTY -- "the single disable switch every downstream V10 check consults, never a second flag" -- on any of: --task omitted; no specs/state.json; the task's entry not found; a missing, empty, null or malformed file_scope; or an internal resolution error. Both recovered paths are absent from task 328's declared file_scope (128 entries, checked at creation time, neither path present), yet both landed in ff880f772. So the follow-up commit reached HEAD past all three sites. Establish WHICH mechanism allowed it -- candidates to TEST, not to assume: --task was omitted on the recovery call, so V10 was disabled outright; or --task was supplied and V10's drop-and-warn posture with exit code 7 ("Observability, not a refusal", per that script's header around line 82) still let the commit stand; or the recovery used a route that does not pass through git-commit-scoped.sh at all. Record the verdict. The structural point survives whichever answer lands: the only route available for recovering a path the containment predicate correctly dropped is a commit that re-asserts no containment.

=== REQUIRED OUTCOMES -- decide and implement ONE coherent rule for each, recording the reasoning ===

1. PREDICATE PARITY AT SITE 1. Site 1 and site 2 test a candidate path by the same rule, with a path-boundary-correct containment test and trailing-slash normalization, so the two sites cannot disagree about the same path against the same declaration. Decide WHERE that rule lives: a shared library function both sites source (the precedent is scripts/lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh, which all three sites already share for the allowlist), or a corrected per-site implementation. Weigh honestly -- the allowlist was consolidated into one library precisely because it had been hand-copied at three sites, and this is the same shape of problem one layer down; but a shared function must preserve each site's own fail-open posture, which differs in detail.

2. SITE 1 INHERITS WHATEVER RULE THE EXTENSION-MANIFEST RECORD LANDS. Once #486 settles its manifest-registration question at site 2, site 1 must reach the same verdict rather than keeping the old behaviour. Decide whether that inheritance is structural (because outcome 1 put the rule in one shared place) or a second explicit edit here. If #486 rules for its own option (3) -- close without a rule, on the grounding that #430's general mechanism subsumes it -- record that site 1 needs nothing on this axis and say so explicitly.

3. A GUARDED RECOVERY ROUTE. Give a dispatch one sanctioned way to land a path the predicate correctly dropped, in which the declaration is extended through the existing mutex-guarded state-write.sh path and the extension is itself recorded, so the recovery commit is checked by the same predicate as the commit that dropped the path. This is the half of the originating change request that #430 does NOT own: #430 decides whether and how a dispatch PROPOSES an addition to its own file_scope; this decides what a dispatch may legitimately COMMIT in the window before that proposal has merged. If the ruling is that the two are inseparable and the recovery route is wholly #430's territory, record that and reduce this record to outcomes 1, 2 and 4 rather than leaving the question open.

4. THE STANDARD STOPS MISDESCRIBING ITSELF. git-staging-scope.md's "Three Containment sites, not one" section no longer claims the three sites run the same predicate when they do not, and records whatever parity outcome 1 lands plus the recovery route outcome 3 lands.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- The containment check exists to stop a concurrently dispatched session's uncommitted edits being swept into the wrong task's commit (git-staging-scope.md's "Concurrency Qualifier: Targeted Staging Is Necessary But Not Sufficient" section, around lines 223-243, records that hazard as observed in production). NO outcome here may weaken it. In particular, fixing site 1's over-matching must TIGHTEN that site, and a guarded recovery route must not become a general bypass.
- Do NOT make any site fatal. Fail-open on a missing, empty or malformed file_scope is deliberate at all three sites and must stay, as must site 1's detection-only, no-exit-code posture for the WORK (h) advisory itself.
- Do NOT weaken drop-and-warn for a genuine excursion. An out-of-territory source edit must still be dropped, warned, and recorded, pinned by a test.
- Do NOT re-introduce or disturb site 2's trailing-slash normalization or the shared engine-written-state allowlist; both are present and working.
- Do NOT widen a task's declared file_scope by hand as the fix, and do not treat the per-task widening used as a workaround elsewhere as a precedent.
- Any state.json write goes through the mutex-guarded state-write.sh path, never a second writer.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- A fixture in test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh proves site 1 and site 2 agree on a shared battery of (declaration, candidate path) pairs, including the trailing-slash directory entry, the boundary case where a declared entry is a string prefix of a NON-child sibling path, and a newly created file under a declared parent directory.
- A fixture proves a genuinely out-of-territory path is still dropped, still warned, and still recorded at site 1.
- A fixture preserves fail-open for a missing, empty and malformed file_scope at site 1.
- The verdict on how ff880f772 landed two non-member paths past all three sites is recorded, with whatever follow-on it implies either fixed here or filed.
- git-staging-scope.md's three-sites section is truthful about the predicates and carries the recovery-route ruling.

=== TERRITORY EDGES -- SEQUENCE, DO NOT PARALLELIZE ===
Dependency edges are declared rather than racing shared files (context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md: shared territory is serialized with an edge, never a bare exclusion).
- #486 and #430: this record's outcome 2 consumes #486's ruling, which in turn depends on #430's general mechanism. Both must settle first; neither reaches site 1.
- #461 and #484: both declare git-commit-scoped.sh (#484 also its test), the surface outcome 3 touches. #484 additionally rewrites the per-path issue-record emission that site 1's sibling sites call.
- #494: the nearest neighbour in SHAPE -- it propagates an own-artifact-directory member that sites 1 and 3 already have to site 2 which never received it. This record is the mirror image, propagating to site 1 what sites 2 and 3 have. Neither subsumes the other and their file_scopes are disjoint, but read it before scoping: its account of the three-site propagation gap is the same account, in the opposite direction.
- #435 (82-path lifecycle-prose sweep) is a strict SUPERSET of this record's declared scope: every path here is already in its file_scope. #448, #472, #476 and in-flight #328 each declare test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh and/or test-git-commit-scoped.sh.

=== BACKLOG AUDIT PERFORMED AT CREATION TIME (scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh, full corpus) ===
The matcher's highest-scoring mechanically-overlapping open records were #486 (semantic 0.69), #494 (0.64), #484 (0.57), #430 (0.51) and #446 (0.50) -- precisely the records read and disclaimed in the scope note above. Ruling rendered by the creating surface, not by the script (which never decides duplication): NOT a duplicate. For #486, #494, #430 and #446 the ONLY mechanically shared path is context/standards/git-staging-scope.md, the standard every containment record necessarily amends; none of the four declares orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, the site where the cited drop fired. #494 is the closest in shape and is the mirror image rather than the same work: it carries a member sites 1 and 3 already have to site 2, where this record carries to site 1 what sites 2 and 3 have. Every remaining non-trivial verdict was a territory overlap on git-commit-scoped.sh, its suite, or test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, and is discharged by a dependency edge above rather than a merge. The matcher additionally emitted 41 scope-blind degradations (corpus records declaring no file_scope, emitted unconditionally per that script's documented noise trade-off) and a long tail of semantic-only verdicts in the 0.40-0.53 band against substantively unrelated records; neither class was treated as a duplication signal.

=== ADDED EVIDENCE (2026-11-10): THREE MORE IN-WINDOW RECOVERIES, AT SITE 2, IN THE CORE REPOSITORY ===

RELEVANCE TO OUTCOME 3, stated without overstating it: these are SITE 2 drops (git-commit-phase.sh), not the site 1 event this record's findings are built on, so they do not bear on outcome 1's predicate-parity question. What they do establish is that the window outcome 3 addresses -- between a correct drop and the postflight merge of the proposed addition -- costs one incomplete commit per occurrence at site 2 as well, three times in one task, and that the only route available for recovering those paths was again a commit outside the containment contract. === SCOPE NOTE: THIS RECORD IS THE UNCOVERED REMAINDER ===

A duplicate check was performed against the open backlog at creation time, using the ownership map an existing record (cycle_postflight_containment_parity) already states for this problem family. That map is accurate and is reproduced here so this record is not re-litigated:
- feed_undeclared_implement_paths_into_file_scope owns the GENERAL in-dispatch file_scope extension channel.
- manifest_registration_dropped_from_phase_commit owns the EXTENSION-MANIFEST half, including the option of treating the touched extension's own manifest.json as implicitly in scope when the same phase adds a file under that extension's scripts/ tree. Its three options -- implicit widening, a pre-commit obligation, or subsumption by the general mechanism -- are the vocabulary this record's half (1) must choose from rather than reinvent.
- close_the_plan_to_file_scope_reconciliation_gap owns the plan-to-file_scope harvest reconciliation and makes a containment drop non-advisory.

- The completed record phase_commit_task_own_artifact_scope_carveout landed the ADJACENT case -- admitting a task's own artifact directory as an implicit containment member, as a per-site splice.
- The completed record allowlist_infrastructure_paths_in_scoped_commits landed the shared engine-written-state allowlist that the three containment sites consult.

What is NOT owned by any of the above, and is this record's subject:

HALF (1) -- WHERE DOES SHARED EXTENSION METADATA BELONG? The dominant path in the citations above is index-entries.json, in three different extensions, NOT manifest.json. The manifest half's narrow option is keyed on a phase adding a file under that extension's scripts/ tree; index-entries.json is written by scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write as a repo-wide line_count sync over CONTEXT files, so that key does not reach it. The obvious candidate home is the engine-written-state allowlist, and the question is genuinely open because that library's own admission bar appears to refuse it. Verified by direct read of agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh at creation time, the bar requires a candidate to be BOTH (a) engine-written on behalf of every/many tasks, not authored by one task's own dispatch, AND (b) never legitimately declarable in any one task's own file_scope. Shared extension metadata satisfies (a) and appears to FAIL (b): a task that adds a context file or a script legitimately declares that extension's index-entries.json or manifest.json in its own file_scope, and several open records do exactly that. The same header's rejected-candidates list refuses task-owned specs/ paths on precisely this reasoning. So decide, with the reasoning recorded:
  (1a) Admit agent-system/extensions/*/index-entries.json (and manifest.json, if the manifest-half record's ruling has not already placed it) to the allowlist, and AMEND the stated admission bar to say why a path that is sometimes legitimately declared still belongs -- do not add a member while leaving a bar that forbids it, which would leave the next author with a contradictory rule.
  (1b) Leave the allowlist alone and resolve this at the sync tool instead: have the tool declare what it touched so the obligation surfaces before the commit rather than as a drop.
  (1c) Rule that the general in-dispatch extension channel subsumes it, record that explicitly, and close half (1) rather than leaving it open.
Read the manifest-half record's ruling first if it has landed; this record's half (1) must agree with it or state why it diverges.

HALF (2) -- THE PROVENANCE HAZARD, unowned by anything above. Quoted from {task 29, iss_1793951759427_sMN8fo}: a commit "staged the WHOLE agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json file via a jq-rewrite-then-commit, which incidentally also committed three unrelated line_count corrections (plan-format.md 882->910, progress-file.md 270->268, metadata-file-return.md 147->143) that reflected OTHER agents' edits to those files, not mine. Verified all three values are objectively correct (wc -l matches). with NO mechanical check anywhere. A phase can close without its own commit and nothing notices --
the deviation surfaces only if the implementing agent volunteers it to its own issue log. The
deliverable is the DETECTION, not a change to the rule.

=== MEASURED EVIDENCE -- READ VERBATIM BEFORE COMPOSING ANYTHING ===

CROSS-REPO CITATION, resolvable against the consumer repository where it was observed:
`~/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/867_formalize_gabbay_separation_ztime/issues.jsonl`, entry_id

    ~/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/867_formalize_gabbay_separation_ztime/issues.jsonl

Its `what_happened` field, verbatim:

  "Phases 18 and 19 both land in ElimHard.lean and were committed together rather than one commit
  per phase. Phase 18 was build-verified green on its own (scoped guarded build, exit 0) before
  Phase 19 began, but no commit was fired at that boundary, so the two cannot now be separated
  without rewriting the file. Deviation from the phase-checkpoint protocol's one-commit-per-phase
  rule."

SILENT is the operative word: Phase 18 was green on its own and a commit was owed at that
boundary; none fired; no gate, script or postflight check registered anything.

=== THE RULE THIS CHECKS ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT IN SCOPE TO CHANGE ===

`context/standards/git-staging-scope.md`'s `### implement` section states it outright: "A plan
phase closes with exactly one commit." `context/contracts/phase-closure.md`'s "Marker/commit
synchrony is bidirectional" section states both directions of the companion marker requirement
(promotion-on-commit, and no-promotion-without-evidence) and records that the over-claim incident
"was caught only because the orchestrator cross-checked the marker count against the working
tree" -- i.e. by an ad hoc human cross-check, not by a mechanism.

THE OBSERVED SHAPE IS A THIRD ONE THAT NEITHER DIRECTION COVERS, and saying so is the point of
this record. Promotion-on-commit requires a phase's marker promotion to ride in the same commit as
that phase's final work; a commit carrying phase 18's promotion AND phase 19's work satisfies that
sentence literally while still violating one-commit-per-phase. No existing contract sentence,
script or test in this source store addresses phase COALESCING. Verified by reading the store:
`skill_corroborate_phase_counts` counts phase headings only, and no script correlates a phase
heading with the existence of that phase's own commit.

=== RECURRENCE -- MEASURED IN THE CONSUMER REPO, RE-DERIVABLE, AND FAR BROADER THAN THE SELF-REPORT ===

The deviation is routine rather than exceptional, and in its commonest form it self-declares in
the commit message. Measured 2026-11-06 in `~/Projects/BimodalLogic` (NOT in this store -- this
store's own history has its own, different population, and the check must be validated against
both). Re-derive rather than trusting these figures:

  git -C ~/Projects/BimodalLogic log --oneline --all --grep="phase [0-9]\+-[0-9]\+" | wc -l
  git -C ~/Projects/BimodalLogic log --format=%s --all --grep="phase [0-9]\+-[0-9]\+" \
    | grep -oE '^task [0-9]+' | sort -u | wc -l

110 commits across 82 DISTINCT tasks carry a coalesced `phase N-M` message, against 6697 total
`phase` commits -- about 1.6%. The originating entry's commit is `8bd45b6ea` ("task 867 phase
18-19: ..."). Coalescing is not limited to adjacent pairs: `9c212620c` coalesces three phases
(`phase 2-4`) and `0688a7a3c` coalesces five (`phase 2-6`). Exactly ONE of those 110 produced an
issue-log entry -- the one cited above. The self-report is the outlier, not the violation. That is
the whole argument for a mechanism, and the reason the per-instance `minor` severity must not be
read as "rare".

=== TWO SHAPES, AND AN HONEST STATEMENT OF WHAT A CHEAP CHECK CATCHES ===

  SHAPE 1, DECLARED. The commit message itself names a range (`task {N} phase 18-19: ...`),
  deviating from the `task {N} phase {P}: {phase_name}` convention in `rules/git-workflow.md`.
  Detectable by reading messages alone -- the signal is already sitting in the data and nothing
  reads it. All 110 measured instances are this shape.

  SHAPE 2, UNDECLARED AND STRICTLY WORSE. A commit names ONE phase while carrying two phases'
  work, or a phase marked `[COMPLETED]` has no `phase {P}` commit at all. A message scan cannot
  see this; it needs the completed-phase markers in the plan cross-checked against the set of
  per-phase commits for that task. Research MUST state which shapes the delivered check covers,
  and MUST NOT let Shape 1 coverage be reported as coverage of the rule.

A plausible economical design, TO BE CONFIRMED OR REJECTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the ingredients
already exist and are already called at postflight. `skill_corroborate_phase_counts` (defined in
`scripts/skill-base.sh`, tested by `scripts/tests/test-corroborate-phase-counts.sh`) already
counts conforming phase headings in a plan, and `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` already
counts a task's commits in a dispatch window via `git log --since` scoped to the task directory
(its `stall_commit_count` derivation). A per-phase commit-existence cross-check -- for every phase
heading marked complete, assert a commit matching `task {N} phase {P}` exists -- reuses both and
catches Shape 2 as well as Shape 1.

  (a) `skill_corroborate_phase_counts` in `scripts/skill-base.sh`. PREFERRED STARTING HYPOTHESIS:

      check lands beside the data it needs.
  (b) `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh`. The natural surfacing point, but the MOST
      CONTENDED file in this store -- open records #472, #476 and #501 all claim it and its test
      suite, and #501 already carries nine dependency edges. If research concludes a call-site
      edit there is unavoidable, declare the edges on those contenders AT THAT POINT rather than
      editing concurrently; per the batching guardrail an unordered overlap gets an edge, never a
      bare exclusion. Prefer a design where the function's existing output line carries the new
      finding so NO postflight edit is needed -- confirm whether that is possible before assuming
      it.
  (c) The phase-closure contract's own gate sequence. Prose only; carries no detection by itself,
      so it is a complement to (a) or (b), never a substitute.

Prefer the cheapest site that catches both shapes. A detection firing only at task postflight is
still worth building even though it cannot un-coalesce an already-landed commit: the measured cost
of the observed instance is irreversibility (the two phases "cannot now be separated without
rewriting the file"), so the realistic value is a named, counted deviation the next dispatch and
the operator can see -- NOT prevention. Do not design for a blocking refusal at the phase-commit
boundary unless research shows it is as cheap AND cannot strand verified-green work; stranding
green work is a worse failure than the deviation it would prevent.

=== TERRITORY -- WHY THE DEPENDENCY EDGES EXIST ===

This record's declared files are claimed by four open records, so it SEQUENCES rather than
excludes (batching guardrail):

A closed record already surfaces a per-cycle scoped commit that was ATTEMPTED AND FAILED

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**. ORIGIN: Conclusion stage (channel b, agent-system changes) of an /orchestrate invocation, session sess_1794023900_f4ac5a. User-approved at the lead level and dispatched to the meta builder for task creation only. CITATIONS: #418:iss_1794001639995_QvyIy9 (the near-miss itself, severity costly); #418:iss_1794001112756_1CPE72 (the partial-stage attempt and its motivation); #418:iss_1794001757595_GJUSiy (a live concurrent sibling writer observed in the same working tree during the same dispatch); #418:iss_1793989293251_3pfJ9z (a plan-time territory collision with a concurrent sibling over a shared file). None of the four carried a suggested_channel hint; routing them to the agent-system channel is the orchestrator's own classification, on the grounds that the hazard lives in shared commit tooling and its governing standard. Severity of the primary entry: costly. PROVENANCE: every file, line number, and quoted string below was re-derived by direct read of the source store at creation time (2026-11-06), not copied from the cited entries. Line numbers move -- re-derive before editing. The incident narrative itself is CARRIED-UNVERIFIED from the cited entries; the mechanism it turns on was independently re-confirmed against the script, as recorded below. LIVE SYMPTOM. A hand-built partial patch was staged with `git apply --cached` against agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json, specifically so that one task's own two hunks would be committed and a concurrent sibling's uncommitted lib/gate-store-fixture-lib.sh provides.scripts line would be left untouched. The subsequent `git commit -- ` nevertheless committed the WORKING-TREE content for that path, sweeping the sibling's unrelated uncommitted line into the commit. It was caught immediately via `git show --stat` and corrected with a second narrow commit removing that line from HEAD, after which the sibling's line was restored into the working tree uncommitted so their in-progress work survived exactly as found. No work was lost. The report is the near-miss and the standing unsoundness, not a live breakage. ROOT CAUSE IS KNOWN GIT SEMANTICS, ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE SCRIPT. scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh's header carries a dedicated block (the "Git semantics discovered empirically while diagnosing V8" note, around lines 259-270) stating that `git commit -- ` RE-READS the current working-tree content fresh for each named path AT COMMIT TIME and does not commit whatever `git add` most recently staged. The index is therefore not the authority for a pathspec commit, and any partial stage of a named path is discarded by the commit that follows. The defect is not that this is unknown; it is that nothing refuses, warns about, or documents the partial-stage idiom that the semantics silently defeat. WHY NO EXISTING GATE CATCHES IT -- VERIFIED, AND THE CRUX TO RULE ON. The V8 post-commit integrity gate (header around lines 164-207; implementation around lines 780-828) takes its PRE-COMMIT INTENT SNAPSHOT as `git hash-object -- "$v8_f"` of each enumerated path's WORKING-TREE content, with an explicit "absent" sentinel when the file is not on disk. V8's operative definition of intent IS therefore the working tree. In the cited incident the working tree held the sibling's line, the commit landed exactly that content, and V8 compared a MATCH -- correctly, by its own contract. V8 structurally cannot see index-vs-working-tree divergence because it never reads the index. The V7 verification loop does read the index, but only for PRESENCE of a path, never for its content. So no gate in the script notices that the caller staged a subset and git committed the superset, and the script exits 0 with nothing printed. THE QUESTION TO RULE ON, NOT A PRESCRIPTION. A defensible outcome here is option (2) -- no code change, documentation only. Do not assume a code change is required. (1) Add a PRE-COMMIT divergence check inside git-commit-scoped.sh: for each surviving positive pathspec, compare the staged content against the working-tree content (per-file index blob vs. `git hash-object`, or `git diff --cached --name-only --

` against `git diff --name-only --

`) and REFUSE, or WARN, when they differ. Refusal is the stronger posture but will also fire on the ordinary and entirely legitimate case of a file edited further after it was staged; decide whether that case is a real population in this pipeline or only an artifact of hand workflows, and record the evidence for whichever answer is given. (2) Change nothing in the script and treat sub-file partial staging as simply UNSUPPORTED, documented as such -- the script's contract then being stated plainly as "for every named path you get the working tree as it stands at commit time". (3) A narrower middle: detect only the specific shape where the index holds a STRICT SUBSET of the working-tree changes for a named path (the partial-stage signature) and warn on that alone, leaving a plain edited-after-staging file unflagged. Options (1) and (3) both interact with V8: if a pre-commit divergence signal exists, V8's own snapshot choice becomes a deliberate, stated decision rather than an unexamined one, and the header must then say which authority each gate consults and why they differ. DOCUMENTATION OBLIGATION, INDEPENDENT OF WHICH OPTION WINS. context/standards/git-staging-scope.md's "Concurrency Qualifier: Targeted Staging Is Necessary But Not Sufficient" section (around lines 223-258) states that "Path granularity is the file -- an explicit-path `git add` cannot subdivide a file by author", then routes the reader to the two sanctioned remedies (the first-claim contended-path lease inside git-commit-scoped.sh, and per-dispatch working-tree isolation). It does NOT name the partial-stage attempt anywhere. A reader who has just been told that granularity is the file will reach for `git apply --cached` as the obvious sub-file workaround, and that reach is silently unsound under `git commit -- `. The section MUST name the trap explicitly: sub-file staging does not survive a pathspec commit, so it is not an available remedy, and the lease and tree isolation remain the only sanctioned ones. WHY THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The same dispatch separately observed a concurrent sibling editing scripts/verify-deploy.sh live, mid-dispatch, in the same working tree (#418:iss_1794001757595_GJUSiy), and a plan-time territory collision with a concurrent sibling over a shared file (#418:iss_1793989293251_3pfJ9z). Concurrent writers in one shared working tree are this repository's normal operating condition, not an exceptional state, which is precisely what makes a silently-unsound narrowing idiom worth closing or naming. DO NOT RE-LITIGATE any of the following: V5's contended-path lease and its first-claim posture; V8's existence, its working-tree snapshot being valuable on its own mechanism-agnostic terms, or its dedicated exit code 5; the prohibition on a bare `git commit`; the settled bare-directory-pathspec policy and its lint. Note also that the incident's own commit was a HAND-RUN `git commit --`, not a git-commit-scoped.sh invocation, so "the script was not involved" is a point for the planner to weigh, not a reason to close the record -- the standard it governs is read by the humans and agents who run git by hand. DEPENDENCY RATIONALE (file territory, not a sequencing preference). Three open records already declare scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh and scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh in their file_scope: task 461 (the V7 refusal of a positive directory pathspec for a `git rm --cached` untracking), whose declared three-file scope is identical to this record's; task 484 (collapsing per-path scope-excursion issue rows); and task 501 (cycle-postflight containment predicate parity). Because this repository runs concurrent writers in one shared working tree -- the very hazard this record reports -- the overlap is sequenced by dependency edges rather than left unordered. Tasks 430, 446 and 486 additionally declare context/standards/git-staging-scope.md but none of the two scripts; that overlap is documentation-only and is deliberately left unsequenced rather than chained, to avoid over-constraining the backlog. PRIOR ART -- DISPOSED OF EXPLICITLY AT CREATION TIME, DO NOT REDISCOVER OR RE-LITIGATE. - Task 374 (completed) is the closest prior art and shares this record's exact three-file scope: it diagnosed and fixed the silent staging drop in git-commit-scoped.sh, and its product IS the V8 gate. It does NOT cover this case, and that distinction is the whole substance of this record. V8's intent authority is the WORKING TREE (`git hash-object` of each enumerated path), so it catches a divergence arising BETWEEN its snapshot and the commit -- a concurrent writer changing the file after staging -- and compares a correct MATCH when the index held a narrower subset than the working tree all along. Read that record's outcome before planning, then state in the plan which authority each gate consults and why. - Task 461 (open) declares a scope identical to this record's three files, for a different defect: the V7 refusal of a positive directory pathspec for a `git rm --cached` untracking whose content is still on disk. Sequenced here by dependency edge. - Task 484 (open) and task 501 (open) both declare git-commit-scoped.sh and its suite -- 484 collapsing per-path scope-excursion issue rows, 501 giving the cycle-postflight containment site predicate parity. Both sequenced by dependency edge for file territory, not for any logical ordering between the subjects. - Tasks 430, 446 and 486 (all open) declare context/standards/git-staging-scope.md but neither script. Documentation-only overlap on one shared file, deliberately left unsequenced. - Task 435 (open) declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ and agent-system/extensions/core/context/ as whole directories for a repo-wide prose reword; that declaration overlaps essentially every agent-system record and is left unsequenced on the same grounds the rest of the backlog leaves it unsequenced. - Closed and settled -- do not reopen: task 302 (the scoped-commit directory pathspec and first-claim task lease), task 199 (the concurrent-dispatch isolation posture decision record, which context/standards/git-staging-scope.md already cites as the home of both sanctioned remedies), task 277 (an unresolvable pathspec made a hard error), task 304 (an out-of-repository pathspec aborting the whole commit, V9), task 226 (staged deletions dropped by the V2 gate). - The creation-time backlog audit returned a cluster of roughly 0.4-to-0.5-scored duplicate-of-open and covered-by-closed verdicts carrying mechanical_class=none against unrelated records. Those are uncorroborated Pass-2 shortlist entries, inflated by this description's length -- the exact condition task 491 (open) exists to fix. They were checked, not accepted. - Task 448 (open) declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ as a whole directory, which covers this record's test suite but neither of its other two files. Its subject -- containing a test harness's deliberate-break mutation of the shared source store -- is unrelated to this one. A single-file overlap inside a broad directory declaration, deliberately left unsequenced: the dependency edges above already serialize this record against every open task that names git-commit-scoped.sh itself.
descriptions.535:
Carve a task's own specs/ artifacts out of git-commit-phase.sh's containment filter, so a task's own plan file is never dropped from its own phase commit.

READ THIS FIRST -- THE DESIGN QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED BY TWO EXISTING CONTRACT TEXTS, AND THIS IS A CODE/CONTRACT DIVERGENCE, NOT A POLICY DECISION. The originating change request asks whether a task's own `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/` artifacts SHOULD be implicitly in scope for its own phase commits rather than requiring explicit `file_scope` declaration. Both documents that specify this filter already say YES, unambiguously and in detail. The implementation does not do it. The work is therefore to make the code match its own already-written specification, plus to correct the one false premise in the standard that let the gap through -- NOT to deliberate the policy afresh.

MEASURED ROOT CAUSE, RE-DERIVABLE IN TWO READS. In `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh` the fixed scope is appended to `stage_paths` first and unconditionally: `stage_paths=("${task_dir}/" "specs/TODO.md" "specs/state.json")`, plus `$plan_path` when `--plan-path` is given. Separately, `files_touched` is DERIVED from `${task_dir}/progress/phase-{P}-progress.json` by unioning `.objectives[].files_touched[]`. The Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check then runs its `is_contained()` predicate over `files_touched` -- and `is_contained()` tests each path ONLY against the entries of the task's declared `file_scope` array. It does not treat `task_dir` as an implicit in-scope member, and it does not carve the four fixed paths out of the loop. The two lists OVERLAP: a path can be both unconditionally staged via `${task_dir}/` and simultaneously present in the derived `files_touched`. When an implementation agent self-reports its own plan artifact in `files_touched` -- which is ordinary, expected behaviour, because the implement phase is supposed to annotate the plan with checklist ticks and phase-heading closure -- that path reaches the filter and is dropped.

THE STANDARD'S OWN STATED REASON WHY THIS CANNOT HAPPEN IS THE FALSE PREMISE. `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md`, in its "Staging-Layer Containment Filter (a Refinement of the Fail-Safe Direction Above)" subsection, asserts: "The four `specs/` carve-out paths (`TASK_DIR/`, `TODO.md`, `state.json`, and the plan path for `implement`) are never tested against this filter at all -- they are appended to the staged set before the filtered loop runs, structurally outside its reach." The conclusion is correct as policy; the stated mechanism is wrong. Being appended to `stage_paths` confers no protection whatsoever on an entry of the SEPARATE `files_touched` list, which is what the loop actually iterates. That sentence is the reason no one noticed the predicate was missing its carve-out, and correcting it is part of this record's deliverable -- a fix that repairs the code while leaving this sentence standing would leave the next reader with the same false assurance.

THE AGENT PROSE, BY CONTRAST, IS ALREADY CORRECT -- DO NOT EDIT IT. `agents/general-implementation-agent.md`'s "Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check" step 2 states the required behaviour exactly: "Carve out of the check entirely: this task's own task directory (`specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/`), `specs/TODO.md`, `specs/state.json`, and the plan path. These four are unconditionally staged by the wrapper and are never themselves task deliverables, so testing them for containment would produce a guaranteed false positive on every single commit." That is the specification the script was ported from and failed to implement. It needs no change; it is the authority the fix should be verified against. Treat any temptation to edit it as a signal that the fix has drifted.

THE REAL COST IS A DISABLED SAFETY GATE, NOT THE WARNING NOISE -- THIS IS MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED. In the observed occurrence the task's phase-1 progress file listed EXACTLY ONE `files_touched` entry, and it was the task's own plan artifact (verify: `jq -r '[.objectives[].files_touched[]?]|unique' specs/771_task_reference_lint_debt_boneyard_tests/progress/phase-1-progress.json` returns a single-element array naming `plans/01_verify-lint-gate-green.md`). The filter dropped that one entry, `kept_files_touched` came back empty, `files_touched` was reassigned to the empty array, and the script therefore set `run_completeness_check=false`. The post-commit completeness check -- the exit-6 detector that this script's own header describes as existing to catch "the exact silent-drop shape this script exists to catch, whatever the underlying mechanism" -- was consequently SKIPPED ENTIRELY for that phase commit. So the failure mode is self-defeating in the worst available way: a false-positive scope drop silently disarms the very gate whose job is to detect silent drops, and it does so precisely in the common case where a phase's only self-reported file is the plan the phase annotated. Any fix MUST be verified to restore `run_completeness_check` in that single-plan-file case, not merely to suppress the warning.

HONEST SEVERITY BOUND -- NO COMMITTED DATA WAS LOST, AND THE RECORD SHOULD NOT CLAIM OTHERWISE. Because `${task_dir}/` is staged unconditionally, the plan file did reach the commit: `git log --oneline --all -- specs/771_task_reference_lint_debt_boneyard_tests/plans/01_verify-lint-gate-green.md` shows it in the phase commit (`task 771 phase 1: verify lint gate green and attribute the fix`) and in the completion commit. The originating entry's `minor` severity is therefore correct for data loss. The three genuine costs are (1) the disabled completeness check above, (2) a false WARNING on stderr that trains readers to discount a warning that is load-bearing for genuine excursions, and (3) a spurious `scope excursion` entry written to `issues.jsonl` via `issue-record.sh`, which then consumed a conclusion-stage channel slot and produced this very record -- a self-inflicted feedback loop whose token cost exceeds the fix's.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS, AND WHY THE TWO ALTERNATIVE SITES ARE WRONG. The request names three candidate sites; evaluate them in this order and record the reasoning.
  (a) `git-commit-phase.sh`'s predicate -- CORRECT SITE. Carve the four fixed paths out before the filtered loop, or equivalently admit `task_dir` plus `specs/TODO.md`, `specs/state.json` and `$plan_path` as implicit in-scope members inside `is_contained()`. Prefer whichever form makes the carve-out visibly parallel to the `stage_paths` construction a few lines above, so the two can be read together. Note that `task_dir` is derived locally in the script already (`task_dir="specs/${padded_num}_${project_name}"`), so the fix needs no new input or lookup.
  (b) `file_scope` declaration/derivation at task creation -- REJECT, with reason recorded. Adding `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/` to every task's declared `file_scope` would make a redundant explicit declaration mandatory forever, on every task, to restate something two contract documents already declare implicit; it would also push synthetic entries into the SEPARATE consumers of `file_scope` -- the Overlap-family contention machinery (`scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh`, `scripts/lib/territory-contention-lib.sh`, `git-commit-scoped.sh`'s V5 contended-path gate) and `scripts/backfill-file-scope.sh` -- which exist to reason about SHARED source-tree territory between tasks, not about a directory only one task can ever own. Keep `file_scope` meaning "the source-tree territory this task may modify".
  (c) `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md` -- NEEDED, BUT AS A CORRECTION, NOT AS THE FIX. The policy there is already right; only the "structurally outside its reach" mechanism sentence is wrong. Replace it with an accurate statement of how the carve-out is actually achieved once (a) lands. Do not restate the policy a third time or introduce a second differently-worded convention.

THE "MAKE IT LOUD" FALLBACK IS MOOT FOR THIS CLASS, BUT MUST NOT BE TRADED AWAY FOR THE OTHER CLASS. The request asks that, if implicit inclusion is rejected, the drop be made loud at minimum. Implicit inclusion is NOT rejected -- it is already the contract -- so for a task's own artifacts the correct end state is no warning and no issue entry at all, because there is no excursion to report. Preserve the existing drop-and-warn behaviour, the `issue-record.sh` call, and the fail-open-on-missing-`file_scope` behaviour UNCHANGED for genuine out-of-scope paths; four such genuine drops are already on record in `specs/754_plan_postflight_file_scope_widening_silent/issues.jsonl` (naming real source-store paths), and those are the filter working as designed. The fix must narrow the predicate's false positives without weakening its true positives.

NO INTERACTION WITH `--allow-out-of-scope` OR THE FILE-SCOPE-WIDENING MECHANISM -- VERIFIED, AND THE NON-INTERACTION SHOULD BE STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. These are three mechanisms at three layers and the fix touches only the first: (i) this containment filter, in `git-commit-phase.sh`, deciding what is PASSED to the commit script; (ii) `--allow-out-of-scope`, which belongs to `scripts/git-snapshot.sh`'s rollback-refusal path, not to the commit path at all; (iii) additive `file_scope` widening at plan postflight, via `scripts/plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` forwarding `--file-scope-add=<json>` to `scripts/update-task-status.sh` (whose merge clause is `(.file_scope) |= ((. // []) + $add | unique)`). Confirm each of these three before writing, and do not route the fix through (ii) or (iii): widening a task's declared `file_scope` to cover its own artifacts is route (b) above under a different name, and is rejected for the same reasons.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) A regression case added to `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh` -- extend the suite, do not replace its existing Case 7 (genuine out-of-scope drop) or Case 8 (fail-open on missing `file_scope`), both of which must stay green and are the guard against over-correction. The new case fixtures a task whose declared `file_scope` names only source paths, whose progress file's sole `files_touched` entry is its own plan artifact under `${task_dir}/`, and asserts all four of: the plan path is NOT dropped; no `dropping out-of-scope path` warning naming it is emitted; no `scope excursion` entry is written for it; and the post-commit completeness check RUNS rather than being skipped. (2) Demonstrate the new case FAILS against the unmodified script before the fix lands -- the current suite is green while the defect is live, so a case that cannot fail first proves nothing. (3) Add coverage for `specs/TODO.md` and `specs/state.json` self-reported in `files_touched` as well; they are exposed by exactly the same gap and the carve-out names them. (4) Redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`.

NON-GOALS. No change to `agents/general-implementation-agent.md` (its prose is the correct specification). No change to the drop-and-warn policy, the `issue-record.sh` integration, or the fail-open direction for genuine excursions. No change to `git-commit-scoped.sh` or any of its V-gates -- the filter is sited one layer above and the exit-code contract is untouched. No retroactive cleanup of the already-written spurious issue entry. No migration of the per-extension implementation agents' hand-typed `stage_paths` arrays to this wrapper; `git-staging-scope.md`'s "Scope of the `git-commit-phase.sh` migration" paragraph already records that as a separately-scoped follow-up and it stays that way. Empty-array expansion under `set -euo pipefail` is safe on bash 4.4 and later (this host runs 5.3), so the existing `"${files_touched[@]}"` expansions need no defensive change -- do not add one.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is silently wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. The owning extension is `core`, whose `source_dir` resolves from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` to `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`. Edit at the mirroring paths there -- `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh`, `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md` -- per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy. The `.claude/**` path in `file_scope` is declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; it is NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors only -- file names, function names (`is_contained`), variable names (`files_touched`, `stage_paths`, `run_completeness_check`), section headings, flag names.

PROVENANCE AND CITATION. Raised by /orchestrate's conclusion stage and approved at the lead level as an agent-system change request, session `sess_1791800175_a20f00`. The originating issue-log entry is `entry_id: iss_1791802976646_M8ywmv` in `specs/771_task_reference_lint_debt_boneyard_tests/issues.jsonl` -- `class: scope excursion`, `severity: minor`, `phase: implement`, `dispatch_seq: null`, `resolution: null`, `evidence_path: null`, `suggested_channel: null`. Because that entry carried no `suggested_channel`, the conclusion stage's assignment to the agent-system channel overrode no hint. Note the entry was written BY the defect itself -- `git-commit-phase.sh`'s own `issue-record.sh` call is its author -- so it is a direct machine-generated artifact of the bug rather than a human report of it, and it should be read verbatim before composing anything. RECURRENCE, STATED HONESTLY: a sweep of every `specs/*/issues.jsonl` in this repository finds exactly ONE occurrence of this own-task-dir false-positive class. It is a single observation; what justifies acting on one observation here is not frequency but structure -- the drop is guaranteed to recur on any phase whose self-reported file set is confined to the task's own annotated plan, and the behaviour contradicts two already-written contract texts rather than merely being undesirable.

ADJACENT OBSERVATION -- A DIFFERENT MECHANISM WITH THE OPPOSITE VISIBILITY, RECORDED SO THE GENERAL SHAPE IS VISIBLE. THIS DOES NOT CHANGE THE ONE-OCCURRENCE RECURRENCE BOUND STATED ABOVE, WHICH REMAINS CORRECT FOR THE OWN-TASK-DIR FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS. Task 727 (`stop_literal_null_file_scope_writes_and_promote_check`, completed 2026-10-03) hit a related phase-commit failure, and conflating the two would mis-scope this record.

WHAT HAPPENED THERE. That task carries TWO `task 727: complete implementation` commits, `2af2fe007` and `59c9abb09`. The second is a recovery commit and says so in its own message: the postflight commit failed because the orchestrator tried to stage the source-store copy of `validate-state.sh`, which lives outside this repository; only the in-repo artifacts were committed, and the source-store edits were left uncommitted in the source store by the implementing agent's deliberate choice, to avoid mixing with unrelated dirty state there. The deliverable did eventually land in the source store and is clean there now (the Check 10 `null_value` promotion text is present), but it landed under `78ab8166e`, "meta: promote the literal-null file_scope finding from WARN to FAIL", which names no task. The consequence is that `git log -- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/validate-state.sh` attributes that file's history to tasks 303, 271, 329 and 279 and to no commit naming 727.

THE THREE WAYS IT DIFFERS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT A SECOND OCCURRENCE OF THE CLASS ABOVE.
  (1) VISIBILITY IS OPPOSITE. The defect this record owns is a SILENT false positive: the path is dropped, the commit succeeds, and the completeness check is disarmed. The 727 case FAILED LOUDLY -- git cannot stage a path outside the repository, so the commit aborted and a human-authored recovery commit followed. A loud failure that produced a recovery commit is not the shape this record exists to fix.
  (2) THE PATH IS NOT IN THE REPOSITORY AT ALL. The own-task-dir class concerns a path that is in-repo but absent from the declared `file_scope`, which is exactly what a carve-out in `is_contained()` fixes. No `file_scope` declaration and no predicate change could admit an out-of-repo source-store path, because the limit is git's, not the filter's.
  (3) THE RESIDUE IS DIFFERENT. This record's cost is a disabled exit-6 completeness check plus a spurious warning and issue entry. The 727 residue is DETACHED PROVENANCE: the work is safe and committed, but it is unattributable to its task from the file's own history.

WHAT THIS RECORD SHOULD DO ABOUT IT: NOTHING IN ITS OWN SCOPE, AND ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT. Do not widen `is_contained()` or the carve-out to admit paths outside the repository -- that cannot work and would be a misreading of this observation. The correct scope stays exactly as specified above. This paragraph exists so that a reader who encounters both symptoms does not merge them into one fix, and so that the provenance gap is on record somewhere; if closing that gap is wanted -- a task whose real deliverable lies in the source store having its source-store commit attributed back to it -- it is its own record, not an extension of this one.

PROVENANCE OF THIS OBSERVATION. Surfaced conversationally while auditing recent task closures in session `sess_1791800175_a20f00`; verified by reading both commit messages, by confirming the promotion text is present and the file clean in the source store, and by `git log -S` locating `78ab8166e` as the commit that introduced it. Not derived from any `issues.jsonl` entry, and no issue entry was written for it.

SECOND OBSERVED OCCURRENCE OF THIS EXACT CLASS, FOLDED IN RATHER THAN FILED SEPARATELY -- AND IT REVISES THE ONE-OCCURRENCE RECURRENCE BOUND STATED ABOVE. descriptions.541:
Stop git-snapshot.sh's --no-revert artifacts from contaminating phase commits with OTHER tasks' files. Two cooperating defects, one in each script; fix the pair, because fixing either alone leaves the contamination reachable.

MEASURED EVIDENCE -- RE-DERIVABLE, DO NOT RE-DERIVE FROM SCRATCH. Commit `b7bba072e` ("task 744 phase 2: wrap RaySummary and KTypeSummary with targeted regeneration") contains 13 files belonging to FOUR unrelated tasks, copied under `specs/744_wrap_inventory_tables_generated_markers/untracked-backup-1792263067/specs/`: `566_possible_worlds_clause_hf_as_limit`, `616_duration_monoid_twisted_arrow_interval_site`, `617_reflection_clause_converse_frame_naturality`, and `785_lean_plan_gate_collision_authoring_guidance`. Verify with `git show --name-only b7bba072e | grep untracked-backup`. Those four directories are STILL untracked in the working tree today, so the repository now carries committed copies of files their owners deliberately left untracked, under a fifth task's directory. They were removed by hand with `git rm` in the phase 3 commit.

DEFECT HALF 1 -- UNSCOPED ENUMERATION, AND THE PLACEMENT THAT EXPOSES IT. In `scripts/git-snapshot.sh`, `--no-revert` mode enumerates untracked files with a bare, REPOSITORY-WIDE `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` and copies every hit to `UNTRACKED_BACKUP="${TASK_DIR}/untracked-backup-${TS}"`. The enumeration is not filtered by the dispatching task's declared `file_scope`, nor by anything else. The sibling `PATCH_PATH="${TASK_DIR}/working-progress-${TS}.patch"` lands in the same place. Both therefore sit INSIDE the dispatching task's own specs directory, which is precisely the directory the phase-commit wrapper stages wholesale.

DEFECT HALF 2 -- THE DIRECTORY PATHSPEC THAT SWEEPS THEM IN, AND WHY NOTHING WARNED. In `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh` the fixed scope is `stage_paths=("${task_dir}/" "specs/TODO.md" "specs/state.json")`, a DIRECTORY pathspec staged first and unconditionally. The script's own header declares this fixed scope "never tested by the Containment Self-Check", so anything sitting in the task directory at commit time is staged with no containment test, no warning, and no `issues.jsonl` entry. That is why the contamination was silent. Note the standing tension with `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`, which forbids a directory-or-glob `git add` pathspec precisely because it "silently pull[s] in concurrent-session or unrelated edits" -- this is that failure, arriving through the wrapper's fixed scope rather than through a hand-typed `git add`.

THE COST IS A SURRENDERED SAFETY MECHANISM, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN NOTING. After reverting the contamination, the implementer stopped taking snapshots for the remaining phases to avoid recurrence. The workaround was to give up the defensive checkpoint. `context/patterns/checkpoint-before-overflow.md` sanctions `--no-revert` as the ordinary defensive checkpoint, and `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md` directs agents to prefer it over the reverting default for exactly this purpose; the defect makes that sanctioned pattern unsafe to use inside any phase-committing dispatch.

RECURRENCE -- BROADER THAN THE ONE CITED COMMIT. `git log --all -- 'specs/*/working-progress-*.patch'` shows the patch half landing in commits across tasks 744, 807, 805 and 794, and `git ls-files 'specs/*/working-progress-*.patch'` shows one still tracked today (under `807_backward_determinism_forcing_check`). The patch sweep is routine, not exceptional. The foreign-file sweep additionally requires foreign untracked files to be present at snapshot time, which is common during multi-task work but not universal.

DESIGN TENSION THAT MUST BE RESOLVED EXPLICITLY, NOT ASSUMED AWAY. The obvious relocation target is the ephemeral gitignored runtime-file class (`specs/.gitignore` carries `**/.orchestration/`, confirmed; the class and its 19 registered members are specified in `context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md`, with patterns in `scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh` and reaping in `scripts/reap-session-runtime-files.sh`). But `git-snapshot.sh`'s own header states a DELIBERATE contrary property: "the marker filename is gitignored (**/.git-snapshot-marker); the durable working-progress-*.patch file is NOT gitignored and remains tracked under the task directory for manual recovery if needed." Relocating the patch into the ephemeral class would convert a deliberately-durable, tracked recovery artifact into an untracked one subject to `reap-session-runtime-files.sh` deletion after `ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_REAP_MIN`. Decide this on the merits and record the reasoning; do not treat the `.orchestration/` candidate as pre-approved. The two artifacts may warrant DIFFERENT answers -- the untracked-backup copies are duplicates of files that are themselves untracked (so making them ephemeral costs little), whereas the patch is the primary durable record of tracked-change state. If the patch stays tracked where it is, then Half 2's exclusion stops being a second line of defense and becomes the whole defense for that artifact, which raises its priority accordingly.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE, IN THIS ORDER.
  (1) Should the untracked backup be scoped to the dispatching task's declared `file_scope` rather than the whole repository? Weigh honestly against the snapshot's stated purpose: `--no-revert` currently reverts nothing, so a narrower backup loses no safety for THIS task, but the default and `--branch` modes DO revert via `git stash push -u`, which sweeps untracked files repository-wide -- so for those modes a repo-wide backup is arguably correct and narrowing it would lose data. Check whether the enumeration is shared across modes before narrowing it in a way that only suits one. Also define the behavior when `file_scope` is absent (many non-terminal tasks declare none) and do not silently fall back to repo-wide copying without saying so.
  (2) Where do the artifacts belong so a directory pathspec cannot reach them? Resolve the durability tension above.
  (3) Does `git-commit-phase.sh`'s fixed-scope pathspec need an explicit exclusion (e.g. a `:(exclude)` magic pathspec for the snapshot artifact names) as a line of defense independent of where the artifacts land? Prefer belt-and-suspenders here given that (2) may leave the patch in place.

ACCEPTANCE -- THE REGRESSION CHECK IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT. Add a case to `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh` and/or `scripts/tests/test-git-snapshot.sh` (both exist in the source store; extend them, do not replace existing cases) that fixtures a repository with foreign untracked `specs/` directories present, runs a `--no-revert` snapshot for one task, then runs that task's phase commit, and asserts NO foreign path is staged or committed. Demonstrate the new case FAILS against the unmodified scripts before the fix lands -- the suites are green while the defect is live, so a case that cannot fail first proves nothing. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`.

NON-GOALS. No retroactive history rewrite to purge the already-committed foreign copies from `b7bba072e` (history rewrites are barred while other writers are live; see `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`). Removing the one still-tracked patch under `807_backward_determinism_forcing_check` is optional cleanup, not required. No change to the guard-hook marker protocol, the single-shot marker consumption, or `git-snapshot.sh`'s stash-identity scheme. No change to `git-commit-scoped.sh` or its V-gate exit-code contract -- both halves sit one layer above it. No change to the containment predicate's treatment of GENUINE out-of-scope paths.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE ADJACENT PHASE-COMMIT RECORD. Task 777 (`phase_commit_drops_own_plan_artifact`) concerns the OPPOSITE direction of the same wrapper: its containment filter false-positively DROPS a task's own plan artifact. This record concerns the fixed-scope pathspec OVER-staging foreign files. They are distinct defects at distinct sites in one file -- 777 edits `is_contained()`, this edits the `stage_paths` construction -- but they share `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh`, and `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md`, so this record declares a dependency on 777 and runs after it rather than concurrently. 777 also corrects a false premise sentence in `git-staging-scope.md` about the fixed scope being "structurally outside [the filter's] reach"; read the CORRECTED text before editing that standard here, and do not reintroduce or re-correct that sentence.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is silently wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. The owning extension is `core`, whose `source_dir` resolves from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` to `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`. Edit at the mirroring paths there -- `scripts/git-snapshot.sh`, `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh`, the two test suites, and any of `context/patterns/checkpoint-before-overflow.md`, `context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md`, `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md`, `scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh` the chosen fix touches -- per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy. The `.claude/**` paths in `file_scope` are declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors only -- file names, variable names (`UNTRACKED_BACKUP`, `PATCH_PATH`, `stage_paths`, `TASK_DIR`), flag names (`--no-revert`), and section headings.

PROVENANCE AND CITATION. `stall_suspected` fires for a dispatch that did no work at all, because its commit probe attributes nothing.

Read `stall_suspected`'s own DELIBERATE NON-WIDENING comment before editing; it is adjacent enough to misjudge. Decide the attribution mechanism and implement it. Candidates, not a mandate: key the probe on the commit message's own task/phase marker; bound the window below by this dispatch's own start rather than relying on `--since` alone; or compare against the commit set already present at dispatch start and count only the delta. Whatever is chosen must also close the postflight-own-commit leak, or state in the code why that leak is acceptable at the canonical site when the record-time site took care to avoid it.

- MUST preserve the commit-gated conjunction as the field's only discrimination (see the DELIBERATE NON-WIDENING comment).

Its open pull request sat at zero reviews for three days, against an unintended base branch. Four earlier per-task branches in the same repository all fork from one identical stale commit because nothing re-pointed them, leaving all four 2150 commits behind the live line. Of those 893,545 insertions, roughly 250,000 are generated or vendored: two hunspell dictionaries at 99,171 lines, dated measurement-run JSON at roughly 70,000, task-management artifacts at 64,641, a baseline ledger at 39,544, a single test fixture at 22,099. The failure mode is repo-agnostic; no part of it depends on that repository's specifics.

=== WHAT TO BUILD (repo-agnostic throughout: no literal branch name, no consumer-repo path, in any deliverable) ===

A. ADMISSION-TIME STARTING-BRANCH VERIFICATION, in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's preflight, beside the existing lock probe and queue-check gates. Resolve the intended integration branch from CONFIGURATION, never a literal: a per-repo declaration site, falling back to the current branch with a loud advisory when undeclared. Follow the advisory-vs-blocking posture the existing predispatch-review defect classes already establish rather than inventing a new one. The depended-on reconciliation task may have ruled that this element also satisfies the dispatch starting-position reverification task -- read its decision record and honor that ruling.

B. PER-INVOCATION BRANCH CREATION, deterministic and idempotent: one branch per orchestrate invocation, cut from the resolved integration branch, named from the invocation's own session identity. Reused rather than recreated when an invocation resumes. Must interact correctly with the existing task-lock, session-registry and orchestration-queue machinery, and must not disturb the MAX_TASKS batch cap or the batching-by-default doctrine in context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md -- preserving batching is a design requirement, since batching is that document's stated default way to work the system.

C. PHASE COMMITS LAND ON THAT BRANCH, with the existing one-commit-per-phase rule and Commit-Per-Green-Substep Mandate granularity fully preserved. Additive: no change to commit SCOPE, pathspec containment, or message convention -- only to branch target. Phase commits from different tasks in one batch interleave on the shared branch, so each commit must remain attributable to its own task; the existing `task {N}: ...` message convention already supplies that, and the design must not weaken it, because element D depends on it.

D. PER-TASK SQUASH LANDING at each task's own [IMPLEMENTING] -> [COMPLETED] transition in orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh: collapse that task's own task-tagged commit range from the invocation branch into ONE commit on the integration branch, message `task {N}: {title}`, with the session identity and the phase list in the body so per-phase detail survives as prose rather than as commits. Per-task ranges on a shared branch are the central mechanical problem of this element -- solve it from commit attribution, not from assuming contiguity. Constraints: never a retroactive rewrite of an already-pushed branch; respect guard-destructive-git.sh (no bare amend, no HEAD-moving reset while another writer is live); prefer `git merge --squash` over interactive rebase, which this environment does not support (`git rebase -i` is unavailable).

E. FAILURE AND PARTIAL RETENTION: a task ending [PARTIAL], [BLOCKED] or failed leaves its commits on the invocation branch un-squashed, so a later invocation resumes from them. Only a clean completion squashes. Define explicitly what happens to an abandoned task's commits and to an invocation branch whose tasks have all landed. State the disposition of a branch holding both a completed task's already-squashed range and a failed task's retained range.

F. GENERATED-FILE DECLARATION for reviewability: a repo-agnostic mechanism declaring machine-written paths so they collapse by default in review (`.gitattributes` with `linguist-generated=true` is the mechanism; the declaration site and whether it is generated or hand-maintained is the design question). The system already knows which paths it generates -- task-management artifacts under specs/, the deployed .claude/** tree, the regenerated task list and roadmap -- so it can declare them rather than asking the operator to enumerate them. Must not change what is COMMITTED, only how it RENDERS in review.

G. DOCUMENTATION PARITY: replace context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md's "## Branch Strategy" section with the mechanically-backed contract this task implements, and add the branch-target rule to rules/git-workflow.md beside its existing granularity rules. A contract that the scripts enforce but the rules do not state is the defect GAP 2 names; do not reproduce it in the other direction.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===

- Repo-agnostic: no literal branch name and no consumer-repo-specific path in any deliverable. Integration-branch identity and branch naming come from configuration.
- git push and pull-request creation stay prohibited for agents (rules/pr-prohibition.md). The deliverable hands the operator a squashed commit on the integration branch; the operator merges to the release branch themselves.
- Must not break the existing lock, session-registry, queue, containment, or snapshot machinery. Additive wherever possible.

- The depended-on reconciliation task's rulings are INPUTS to this task, not suggestions: read its decision record during research and honor its prerequisite, revision and detector-scope rulings.
- Size realistically. This spans two orchestration scripts, two commit scripts, one rule file and two standards documents, and it changes a contract every phase commit in every repository flows through. Expect systematic refactoring; do not plan it as a one-file change.

VERIFICATION. A multi-task invocation produces one branch, phase commits from every task on it, and one squashed commit per completed task on the integration branch with its phase list in the body. A task failing mid-batch leaves its commits on the branch while its sibling still lands. An invocation started from the wrong branch is caught at admission. The declared generated paths render collapsed in review. The rules and the narrative state the same contract the scripts enforce.

A proposal that merely asserts a better design, or that does not engage the recorded mechanism, is out of order. Re-reaching the same verdict is a perfectly acceptable outcome; reaching any verdict without reading the evidence is not.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER: the best git workflow for working off a long-lived feature branch using side branches and squash merging as appropriate, to produce the highest-quality history, with milestones as the natural points at which work is submitted for review.

START FROM MEASURED FACT, NOT PROSE. Orchestration today has ZERO branch awareness: across the core extension's scripts/ and hooks/, `grep -rn "git checkout -b\|git switch -c"` returns exactly one hit, inside git-snapshot.sh's --branch rollback path, which is a recovery feature rather than a workflow. === ELEMENT 2 ONWARD -- THE AUTOMATION AND REVIEW GATES ===

Built on Element 1's ruling and on the milestone schema from this task's dependency:

- An orchestration completing updates its milestone's progress in specs/state.json and regenerates ROADMAP.md.
- A batch's orchestrations all completing initiates systematic testing.
- A milestone completing initiates the git push and review stage.
- context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md's Branch Strategy prose is reconciled with whatever mechanical model Element 1 settles, so the written standard and the enforced behaviour agree.

THE PUSH GATE MUST USE THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND MUST NOT VIOLATE THE PROHIBITION. rules/pr-prohibition.md bars agents from pushing and from creating PRs/MRs. The archived task `consent_gated_git_push` already built the sanctioned exception end to end: hooks/guard-git-push.sh (PreToolUse push guard plus tamper guard), hooks/please-grant.sh (a UserPromptSubmit hook minting single-use HMAC-signed grants ONLY from a literal human prompt), scripts/git-push-granted.sh (the sanctioned wrapper), and the user-invoked /please command. A milestone-completion review stage must therefore PREPARE the push and the review request and hand them to the user through that existing grant path -- never mint its own grant, never infer permission from a milestone being complete, and never push or open a PR autonomously. Design it as preparation plus a handoff, and say so explicitly in the deliverable.
